title: In 1933 the US ordered its citizens to hand in their gold
body: On 5 April 1933, President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed Executive Order 6102, forbidding the hoarding of gold coin, bullion and gold certificates in the continental United States. Americans had to deliver most of their gold to the Federal Reserve by 1 May and were paid **$20.67 per troy ounce**; breaking the order risked a $10,000 fine or ten years in prison. The aim was to free the Federal Reserve, whose notes needed 40% gold backing, to expand the money supply during the Depression. In 1934 the Gold Reserve Act set the price at $35 an ounce, and private gold ownership became legal again only at the end of 1974.

slides.question: The official price went from $20.67 to $35 an ounce in 1934. By what percentage did gold’s dollar price rise?
slides.explanation: From $20.67 to $35 is a rise of about 69%. The dollar was worth that much less in gold, which gave the Federal Reserve room to expand the money supply.

slides.heading: Why?
slides.text: The Federal Reserve Act of 1913 required 40% gold backing for the notes the Fed issued, and by the late 1920s it had nearly reached the limit of credit it could extend. Taking gold out of private hands and then repricing it loosened that constraint.
